evidence.title: Kernel Auto-Selection v2 — Override and Rollback Runbook
evidence.text:
egime
Common signatures:
- Long-context prefill (e.g., prefill tokens > 8k) getting a kernel optimized for short prompts
- Mixed workloads: frequent switching between prefill/decode-heavy traffic

### C) Validate with logs (sample)
Search runtime logs for selection event:
- `kernel_selection_v2 decision` OR `selector_v2 chosen_kernel=`

If telemetry sampling is low, temporarily increase sampling for a narrow scope (model+region) only (see "Optional: increase telemetry sampling").

---

## Step 1 — Disable v2 (narrow scope)
Disabling v2 means: selector falls back to v1 behavior.

### 1A) Disable v2 for a specific model in a region (Hosted)
Use when a single model regresses.

Command:
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --model llama-3-70b-instruct --value off`

Verify:
- `rwctl runtime gates get kernel_autoselect_v2 --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --model llama-3-70b-instruct`

Notes:
- Changes should propagate within ~2–5 minutes.
- If propagation stalls, trigger safe config reload (Step 4).

### 1B) Disable v2 for a GPU SKU in a region (Hosted)
Use when regressions are tied to a hardware type.

Command:
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --gpu-sku nvidia-l40s --value off`

### 1C) Disable v2 for a Dedicated pool
Use when a Dedicated pool has a constrained GPU type or a customer escalation.

Command:
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env dedicated --pool ded-pool-northstar-a100 --value off`

If you need to scope it further:
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env dedicated --pool ded-pool-northstar-a100 --model qwen2-72b-instruct --value off`

### 1D) Disable v2 for Private deployments
Private customers may have pinned driver/CUDA versions; treat this as customer-impacting.

Command (if customer uses managed control plane):
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env private --tenant northwind-analytics --value off`

If the customer is air-gapped/on-prem, coordinate with Support/CS and provide them the config snippet (see "Private/on-prem config snippet").

---

## Step 2 — Denylist known-bad combinations (preferred for error spikes)
Use denylisting when the issue is tied to a **kernel+SKU** combination causing errors.

Example:
- Denylist `flash-attn-v3` on `nvidia-l40s` for all models in `us-east-1`.

Command:
- `rwctl runtime kernel-registry deny --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --gpu-sku nvidia-l40s --kernel flash-attn-v3 --reason "launch failures after 1.21 canary" --ttl 72h`

Notes:
- Prefer a TTL for emergency mitigation so it is automatically revisited.
- Denylisting should force selector v2 to choose the next safe fallback; if that is insufficient, disable v2 for that SKU.

---

## Step 3 — Pin a kernel (temporary mitigation)
Pinning is a faster workaround when v2 is enabled but picking the wrong kernel for a specific regime.

**Use pinning when:**
- Latency regression is due to mis-selection, not crashes
- You have a known-good kernel from prior benchmarks

**Avoid pinning when:**
- You see runtime errors / correctness concerns
- You are unsure which kernel is safe for that SKU

### 3A) Pin by model + SKU + sequence regime bucket
Common buckets:
- `prefill_short` (<= 2k prefill tokens)
- `prefill_medium` (2k–8k)
- `prefill_long` (> 8k)
- `decode_heavy` (high decode tokens)

Command:
- `rwctl runtime kernel-pin set --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --model llama-3-70b-instruct --gpu-sku nvidia-a100-80gb --seq-bucket prefill_long --kernel fused-prefill-v2 --ttl 24h --reason "p99 long-context regression; workaround"`

### 3B) Emergency runtime flag (last resort, debugging only)
If you need a one-off reproduction on a canary pod:
- Set the runtime flag via deployment override (do NOT do fleet-wide without Kernels approval):
  - `--force_kernel=fused-prefill-v2`
  - `--dump_kernel_selection=true`

This is for containment and debugging. Prefer config-based pins for productio

evidence.text:
description:
Context
Kernel auto-selection v2 is being rolled out behind gates. Current perf suite coverage under-represents long-context prompts (large prefill) and mixed prompt distributions that stress selector stability + batching/scheduling interactions. We also need explicit pass/fail thresholds for canary/GA decisions so we don’t debate “is this regression acceptable?” during rollout.

Goals
1) Expand benchmark coverage to include long-context and mixed workloads that match Dedicated/Private customer usage (summarization, RAG over long docs, batchy micro-prompts, and mixed prefill/decode ratios).
2) Define pass/fail thresholds for v2 vs v1 per (model family, seq-bucket regime, GPU SKU) and provide a single “canary gate” summary.
3) Ensure runs are reproducible/deterministic enough to catch tail-latency spikes (p95/p99) without flakiness.

Non-goals
- Not building a full eval/quality harness (handled by Perf & Evals separately).
- Not tuning selector thresholds here (that stays in selector PRs); this ticket only expands measurement + gating.

What to add (coverage)
A) Long-context scenarios (prefill-heavy)
- Context lengths: 8k, 16k, 32k tokens (where model supports), with decode lengths: 64, 256.
- Measure TTFT (time-to-first-token), prefill latency, and p95/p99 for first token + steady-state decode.
- Include at least one “near-memory-limit” prompt (but safe) to surface kernel choices that increase peak memory.

B) Mixed workloads (selector stability + scheduling interaction)
- Mix distributions within a single run (same worker pool):
  - 70/20/10 short/medium/long (e.g., 512/2k/16k prefill) with decode 128.
  - 50/50 interactive vs batchy (short requests with concurrency spikes vs medium requests with steady concurrency).
- Add “two-peak” distribution (most requests small, occasional very long) to replicate tail amplification.
- Ensure selector gets consistent features: model family tag, seq-bucket, GPU SKU; record selection decisions for correlation.

C) Model family coverage (minimum set for gating)
- Llama family (e.g., Llama-3 class)
- Mistral family
- Qwen family
- Gemma family
Note: the actual model IDs used in perf suite should follow the existing benchmark-lab naming + availability per GPU.

D) GPU SKUs (minimum set)
- A100 80GB
- H100 (SXM where available; PCIe acceptable if that’s what benchmark-lab has)
- L40S
- If available in lab: A100 40GB (or MIG slice) as “constrained memory” signal.

Metrics to record (must-have)
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for TTFT, end-to-end, and per-token decode (where supported).
- Throughput: tokens/sec (decode), requests/sec, and effective batch size distribution.
- Error/health: OOM rate, kernel launch failures, retried requests (if visible), and % fallback kernel usage.
- Selector telemetry correlation keys: selected_kernel, candidate_set_size, seq_bucket, gpu_sku_norm, model_family, selector_version, gate_state (v1/v2).

Pass/Fail thresholds (proposed for runtime-1.21 rollout)
Definitions
- Baseline is selector v1 on same commit (or closest stable) and same environment.
- Compare v2 vs v1 per (model family × scenario × GPU SKU). Use same seeds and at least N=5 repetitions; aggregate by median of runs for p95/p99 to reduce flake.

Hard fail (block canary expansion / trigger rollback recommendation)
- p99 end-to-end latency regression > +8% in any long-context scenario on any “supported” GPU SKU.
- p95 TTFT regression > +10% in long-context (16k/32k) scenarios.
- Error rate increase > +0.25% absolute (OOMs, launch failures) in any scenario.
- Fallback rate (to “safe” kernel) increases by > +15% absolute without corresponding error improvements (indicates mis-selection / denylist gaps).

Soft fail (requires sign-off from Runtime Architect + SRE before proceeding)
- p99 regression between +5% and +8% in any scenario.
- p95 regression between +3% and +5% in mixed workloads.
- Increased variance/run-to-run instability: coefficient of variation (CoV) for p99 > 0.12 across repetitions, u

evidence.title: Fix long-context regression: adjust prefill regime thresholds to avoid tail-latency spikes
evidence.text:
e 1.21, we saw a p99 regression on long-context workloads (>=16k prompt tokens) on L40S and some A100 pools when kernel auto-selection v2 classified certain requests into the “mid” prefill bucket and chose FA3 prefill variants that are great for short/mid contexts but showed allocator/workspace churn at long context (and worse tail when batch composition is mixed). This PR tightens the v2 rules to prevent mis-selection in the long-context regime while keeping determinism guarantees and preserving the gains on short/mid prompts. Changes: (1) Adjust prefill-length bucket boundaries and add a small hysteresis band to reduce flip-flopping around thresholds when scheduler-provided distribution hints are noisy. (2) Add an explicit long-context guard: for ctx >= LONG_CTX_TOKENS (default 12288), prefer the “lc_prefill” kernels when available, otherwise fall back to the known-stable v1-equivalent prefill path. (3) Add SKU-aware exception for L40S where the problematic kernel variant was disproportionately impacting tail; we now require a stricter threshold before selecting it and we prefer the stable alternative when decode_len is small (prefill-dominant requests). (4) Add unit tests covering boundary conditions + replay determinism around bucket edges, including cases with mixed scheduler hints. Bench results: See attached before/after plots from perf suite run 2026-02-14 and canary replay slice. Summary on L40S (long-context summarization profile, 16k/256): p95 1.38s -> 1.11s (-19.6%), p99 2.74s -> 1.63s (-40.5%). On A100 (same profile): p95 1.02s -> 0.98s (-3.9%), p99 1.88s -> 1.61s (-14.4%). No correctness diffs observed (golden outputs match within expected nondeterminism bounds; selection remains deterministic for fixed inputs). Notes: This is intended as a targeted rule tweak; no changes to telemetry schema. Rollout: safe to land in release/1.21 behind existing gates; recommended to promote to Hosted canary first, then Dedicated pools after 24h with the rollout dashboard guardrails. Artifacts/plots: Before/after plot bundle: gs://redwood-perf-artifacts/kernel-select-v2/28522-longctx-prefill-thresholds/plots/index.html ; Comparison table: gs://redwood-perf-artifacts/kernel-select-v2/28522-longctx-prefill-thresholds/summary.csv . Checklist: [x] Adds/updates unit tests for bucket boundaries and long-context guard [x] Verifies selector determinism tests still pass [x] Runs perf suite subset (Llama/Mistral long-context + mixed) on A100 + L40S [x] Confirms no telemetry cardinality changes [x] Updates release/1.21 notes comment (see thread) to mention long-context fix (internal) [x] Linked SUP-31842 for traceability

evidence.text:
issues index
| ID | Severity | Symptom | Affected | Status | Recommended mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| KASV2-001 | High | p99 regression on long-context prefill | Llama-family long-context (>16k) on mixed fleets | Mitigated via rule tweak; watchlist | Disable v2 for model in region; or force prefill kernel fallback |
| KASV2-002 | High | Kernel crash / CUDA illegal memory access | L40S + driver 535.x + FlashAttn v3 path | Active (denylisted) | Denylist kernel on SKU+driver; pin to FA2 fallback |
| KASV2-003 | Medium | Throughput jitter on mixed workloads | H100 pools with rapidly shifting seq regime | Active (needs tuning) | Enable scheduler seq-distribution hints; increase decision cache TTL |
| KASV2-004 | Medium | Non-deterministic selection across replicas | MIG partitions / inconsistent SKU strings | Active (guardrail) | Normalize SKU; disable v2 when `gpu_partitioned=true` until normalized |
| KASV2-005 | Medium | FP8 decode instability / quality drift | H100 FP8 decode kernels on specific model variants | Active (allowlist-only) | Keep kernels allowlisted per model revision; fall back to BF16 |
| KASV2-006 | Low | Telemetry cardinality / dashboard noise | High model+kernel combinations during canary | Mitigated | Reduce sampling; aggregate candidate set; update queries |

---

## Detailed issues

### KASV2-001 — Long-context prefill mis-selection causing tail latency spikes
**Severity:** High (SLO risk)

**Symptom**
- p95 stable but **p99 spikes** (often +25–80%) for long-context workloads.
- Spikes correlate with requests where prefill tokens exceed the selector’s long-context threshold.

**Affected**
- Model families: Llama variants (including instruct), some Qwen long-context fine-tunes.
- Workload: prefill >16k tokens, or mixed traffic where the long-context share is low but impactful.
- Fleets: more pronounced on heterogeneous fleets (A100 + L40S) due to differing kernel sweet spots.

**Likely cause**
- Seq-length regime bucketing for prefill was too permissive in mixed workloads; selector chose a kernel optimized for mid-length prefill which has worse tail behavior at >16k.

**Detection signals**
- Selector telemetry shows `seq_bucket=prefill_mid` or `prefill_decode=mixed` even when observed prefill tokens are in the long bucket.
- Latency delta panel spikes only for `seq_bucket` transitions.

**Workarounds (approved)**
1) **Disable v2 for the affected model in the affected region** (preferred for immediate stabilization).
2) **Force/pin prefill kernel** for the model on the affected SKU(s) if disabling v2 is too broad.
3) **Temporary allowlist restriction**: only enable v2 for that model on GPU SKUs where long-context kernel has been validated.

**Notes / follow-ups**
- This is partially addressed by threshold updates shipped during Runtime 1.21 canary tuning. Still a watchlist item due to workload diversity.

**Last verified**: 2026-02-21

---

### KASV2-002 — L40S + driver 535.x crash on FlashAttention v3 kernel path
**Severity:** High (correctness + availability)

**Symptom**
- Occasional worker crash with:
  - `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`
  - or `misaligned address` originating from attention kernel launch.

**Affected**
- GPU SKU: L40S (not consistently reproducible on A100/H100)
- Driver/CUDA: NVIDIA 535.x (most reports on 535.129–535.161)
- Kernel family: FlashAttention v3 attention kernels (prefill + decode variants)

**Likely cause**
- Driver interaction with FA3 kernel variant under specific head dimensions / rotary embedding settings.

**Workarounds (approved)**
- **Hard denylist** the FA3 kernel variants for `gpu_sku=L40S` when `driver_major=535`.
- Fallback to FA2 or baseline attention kernels per ADR fallback precedence.
- If Dedicated/Private cannot change drivers quickly: keep denylist and plan driver upgrade.

**Operational guidance**
- If crash rate > 0.1% of requests on the pool, treat as rollback trigger for v2 on that pool.

**Last verified**: 2026-02-25

description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports p99 latency regression for long-context summarization workloads immediately after we enabled Runtime 1.21 canary on their Dedicated pool. Regression appears only for long-context requests (>= ~16k prompt tokens) and only on NVIDIA L40S.

Impact
- Customer-visible tail latency increase on long-context routes.
- Reported baseline (Runtime 1.20 / selector v1): p99 ~4.8–5.4s @ ~20k prompt tokens, 256–512 decode tokens.
- After canary (Runtime 1.21 / selector v2 enabled): p99 ~8.9–10.6s for same workload; p50/p90 mostly unchanged.
- No correctness issues reported. Error rate stable.

Customer context
- Northwind Analytics uses Redwood Dedicated for long-context summarization (document ingestion + map-reduce style prompts). Workload is bursty but within reserved throughput.

Environment
- Dedicated pool: nw-analytics-ded-01
- Region: us-east
- GPU SKU: NVIDIA L40S (SM89)
- Driver/CUDA: 550.54.14 / CUDA 12.4
- Runtime: 1.21.0-canary.3
- Feature: Kernel auto-selection v2 enabled via canary gate for Llama family

2) Observe p99 latency increase vs previous runtime.
3) Short prompts (<4k) appear unaffected.

evidence.title: Fix long-context regression: adjust prefill regime thresholds to avoid tail-latency spikes
evidence.text:
description:
Context: During perf characterization + Hosted canary for runtime 1.21, we saw a p99 regression on long-context workloads (>=16k prompt tokens) on L40S and some A100 pools when kernel auto-selection v2 classified certain requests into the “mid” prefill bucket and chose FA3 prefill variants that are great for short/mid contexts but showed allocator/workspace churn at long context (and worse tail when batch composition is mixed). This PR tightens the v2 rules to prevent mis-selection in the long-context regime while keeping determinism guarantees and preserving the gains on short/mid prompts. Changes: (1) Adjust prefill-length bucket boundaries and add a small hysteresis band to reduce flip-flopping around thresholds when scheduler-provided distribution hints are noisy. (2) Add an explicit long-context guard: for ctx >= LONG_CTX_TOKENS (default 12288), prefer the “lc_prefill” kernels when available, otherwise fall back to the known-stable v1-equivalent prefill path. (3) Add SKU-aware exception for L40S where the problematic kernel variant was disproportionately impacting tail; we now require a stricter threshold before selecting it and we prefer the stable alternative when decode_len is small (prefill-dominant requests). (4) Add unit tests covering boundary conditions + replay determinism around bucket edges, including cases with mixed scheduler hints. Bench results: See attached before/after plots from perf suite run 2026-02-14 and canary replay slice. Summary on L40S (long-context summarization profile, 16k/256): p95 1.38s -> 1.11s (-19.6%), p99 2.74s -> 1.63s (-40.5%). On A100 (same profile): p95 1.02s -> 0.98s (-3.9%), p99 1.88s -> 1.61s (-14.4%). No correctness diffs observed (golden outputs match within expected nondeterminism bounds; selection remains deterministic for fixed inputs). Notes: This is intended as a targeted rule tweak; no changes to telemetry schema. Rollout: safe to land in release/1.21 behind existing gates; recommended to promote to Hosted canary first, then Dedicated pools after 24h with the rollout dashboard guardrails. Artifacts/plots: Before/after plot bundle: gs://redwood-perf-artifacts/kernel-select-v2/28522-longctx-prefill-thresholds/plots/index.html ; Comparison table: gs://redwood-perf-artifacts/kernel-select-v2/28522-longctx-prefill-thresholds/summary.csv . Checklist: [x] Adds/updates unit tests for bucket boundaries and long-context guard [x] Verifies selector determinism tests still pass [x] Runs perf suite subset (Llama/Mistral long-context + mixed) on A100 + L40S [x] Confirms no telemetry cardinality changes [x] Updates release/1.21 notes comment (see thread) to mention long-context fix (internal) [x] Linked SUP-31842 for traceability

review_conversation:
Hiro Tanaka (review): The guard looks right, but I’m worried about thrash around the boundary when scheduler hints are “mostly long” but a single request is 8–10k. Can we ensure we don’t oscillate between kernels within the same warm pool? Also please justify the 12288 default. Yuki Sato (author): Added hysteresis band using a two-threshold approach when distribution_hint is present (enter long_ctx at 12k, exit at 10k) to reduce oscillation. Default 12288 matches the prefill workspace knee we saw in perf plots across L40S and A100; linked plot bundle in description. Lena Fischer (review): For mixed workloads, can you include decode_len in the guard? Some of the worst spikes were prefill-dominant. Yuki Sato: Updated rule ordering so the long_ctx guard checks (ctx_tokens >= 12288 && decode_tokens <= 512) before the generic bucket-based choice, which matches the spike signature. Omar El-Sayed (review): Please confirm we’re not changing telemetry cardinality; last week’s incident thread was noisy. Also add a log-only counter for how often this guard triggers so we can validate during rollout. Yuki Sato: No schema changes. Added a single aggregated counter kernel_select_v2.long_ctx_guard_triggered (no extra tags beyond existing model_family/gpu_sku/region sampling policy). Marcus Reed (review): Bench numbers look good, but I’d like to see at least one run on Qwen long-context profile as well. Yuki Sato: Added Qwen2.5-14B long-context run results to the same artifact bundle; deltas are neutral-to-positive (p99 -9% on L40S). Allison Grant (review): Can we add a short note to release/1.21 internal notes so oncall knows this is the fix for SUP-31842? Yuki Sato: Added a brief entry under “Kernel selection v2” in the internal known-issues/release notes file. Approvals: Hiro (approved), Lena (approved), Omar (approved), Marcus (approved).

evidence.title: Kernel Auto-Selection v2 — Override and Rollback Runbook
evidence.text:
## Purpose
This runbook describes how oncall can safely override or roll back **Kernel Auto-Selection v2** ("selector v2") when it causes tail-latency regressions, stability issues, or correctness risks. It covers:
- Disabling v2 by **model**, **GPU SKU**, and/or **region** (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)
- Pinning a specific kernel (temporary mitigation)
- Safe rollback procedure (fast + staged)
- Validation steps using dashboards and logs

**Primary goals:** restore p95/p99 latency and error rates to baseline while preserving correctness and preventing fleet-wide disruption.

---

## Scope / when to use
Use this runbook when any of the following are true during canary or production:
- p99 latency regression attributed to kernel selection (common: long-context prefill misclassification)
- Elevated runtime errors (CUDA illegal memory access, miscompiled kernel, launch failures) correlated with a chosen kernel/SKU
- Throughput instability or jitter that correlates with selection distribution changes
- Customer escalation requiring immediate mitigation (Dedicated/Private pools with constrained SKUs)

**Do not use** this runbook for general GPU/node instability, scheduler overload, or non-kernel runtime crashes unless kernel selection has been implicated.

---

## Ownership / escalation
**Oncall owns mitigation**, Runtime Kernels owns root cause.

- Runtime Oncall: #eng-oncall (primary)
- Runtime Kernels: #eng-runtime (paging if rollback required)
- SRE: #eng-sre (paging if SLO breach / incident)
- Releases: #eng-releases (if changes impact runtime 1.21 rollout windows)

Escalate immediately if:
- Any correctness regression suspected (bad outputs, determinism broken)
- Crash-looping exceeds 2% of pods in a region/pool
- You need to disable v2 globally in Hosted prod

---

## Preconditions / access
You need:
- Access to **Control Plane feature gates** and runtime config (prod breakglass if applicable)
- Dashboard access (Kernel Selection v2 Rollout dashboards)
- Log access for serving runtime pods

Tools referenced:
- `rwctl` (Redwood internal CLI)
- Runtime admin endpoint (read-only + safe config reload)

If `rwctl` is unavailable, use the Control Plane Console: **Console → Runtime → Feature Gates**.

---

## Definitions
- **v1**: existing kernel selection behavior (baseline)
- **v2**: kernel selection logic keyed on model family + sequence regime + GPU SKU
- **Gate**: enable/disable selector v2
- **Allowlist / denylist**: model- or SKU-scoped enablement rules
- **Pin**: force a specific kernel choice (override), bypassing selector ranking

### Canonical identifiers
Use canonical forms to avoid mismatches:
- **Region:** `us-east-1`, `us-west-2`, `eu-central-1`
- **GPU SKU:** normalized string e.g. `nvidia-a100-80gb`, `nvidia-h100-sxm`, `nvidia-l40s`
- **Model ID:** `llama-3-70b-instruct`, `mistral-large-2407`, `qwen2-72b-instruct`, `gemma-2-27b-it`

If SKU naming is ambiguous (MIG / cloud instance mapping), see: "GPU SKU normalization" in the debugging playbook.

---

## Quick decision tree (2 minutes)
1) **Is this isolated to one model OR one SKU OR one region?**
   - Yes → Disable v2 narrowly (model/SKU/region) OR pin kernel
   - No → Disable v2 at environment scope (Hosted prod or pool-wide) and page Runtime Kernels

2) **Are there runtime errors (not just latency)?**
   - Yes → Prefer **denylisting** the kernel/SKU combination (or disabling v2 for that SKU) rather than pinning.

3) **Is there a customer impact in Dedicated/Private?**
   - Yes → Prefer **pool-specific** disable or pin; avoid global Hosted changes unless needed.

---

## Primary levers
You have four safe mitigation levers (in preferred order):
1) **Disable v2 for a model in a region** (least blast radius)
2) **Disable v2 for a GPU SKU in a region/pool**
3) **Pin a kernel for a model+SKU+seq bucket** (fast workaround, higher risk)
4) **Disable v2 globally** (largest blast radius; requires notification)

---

## Step 0 — Confirm it is selector v2
Before changing gates, confirm correlation:

### A) Check selection distribution shift
Dashboard panel: **Selection distribution by kernel (model/SKU/seq bucket)**
- Look for a sudden rise in a kernel correlated with a latency spike.

### B) Confirm the request regime
Common signatures:
- Long-context prefill (e.g., prefill tokens > 8k) getting a kernel optimized for short prompts
- Mixed workloads: frequent switching between prefill/decode-heavy traffic

### C) Validate with logs (sample)
Search runtime logs for selection event:
- `kernel_selection_v2 decision` OR `selector_v2 chosen_kernel=`

If telemetry sampling is low, temporarily increase sampling for a narrow scope (model+region) only (see "Optional: increase telemetry sampling").

---

## Step 1 — Disable v2 (narrow scope)
Disabling v2 means: selector falls back to v1 behavior.

### 1A) Disable v2 for a specific model in a region (Hosted)
Use when a single model regresses.

Command:
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --model llama-3-70b-instruct --value off`

Verify:
- `rwctl runtime gates get kernel_autoselect_v2 --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --model llama-3-70b-instruct`

Notes:
- Changes should propagate within ~2–5 minutes.
- If propagation stalls, trigger safe config reload (Step 4).

### 1B) Disable v2 for a GPU SKU in a region (Hosted)
Use when regressions are tied to a hardware type.

Command:
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --gpu-sku nvidia-l40s --value off`

### 1C) Disable v2 for a Dedicated pool
Use when a Dedicated pool has a constrained GPU type or a customer escalation.

Command:
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env dedicated --pool ded-pool-northstar-a100 --value off`

If you need to scope it further:
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env dedicated --pool ded-pool-northstar-a100 --model qwen2-72b-instruct --value off`

### 1D) Disable v2 for Private deployments
Private customers may have pinned driver/CUDA versions; treat this as customer-impacting.

Command (if customer uses managed control plane):
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env private --tenant northwind-analytics --value off`

If the customer is air-gapped/on-prem, coordinate with Support/CS and provide them the config snippet (see "Private/on-prem config snippet").

---

## Step 2 — Denylist known-bad combinations (preferred for error spikes)
Use denylisting when the issue is tied to a **kernel+SKU** combination causing errors.

Example:
- Denylist `flash-attn-v3` on `nvidia-l40s` for all models in `us-east-1`.

Command:
- `rwctl runtime kernel-registry deny --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --gpu-sku nvidia-l40s --kernel flash-attn-v3 --reason "launch failures after 1.21 canary" --ttl 72h`

Notes:
- Prefer a TTL for emergency mitigation so it is automatically revisited.
- Denylisting should force selector v2 to choose the next safe fallback; if that is insufficient, disable v2 for that SKU.

---

## Step 3 — Pin a kernel (temporary mitigation)
Pinning is a faster workaround when v2 is enabled but picking the wrong kernel for a specific regime.

**Use pinning when:**
- Latency regression is due to mis-selection, not crashes
- You have a known-good kernel from prior benchmarks

**Avoid pinning when:**
- You see runtime errors / correctness concerns
- You are unsure which kernel is safe for that SKU

### 3A) Pin by model + SKU + sequence regime bucket
Common buckets:
- `prefill_short` (<= 2k prefill tokens)
- `prefill_medium` (2k–8k)
- `prefill_long` (> 8k)
- `decode_heavy` (high decode tokens)

Command:
- `rwctl runtime kernel-pin set --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --model llama-3-70b-instruct --gpu-sku nvidia-a100-80gb --seq-bucket prefill_long --kernel fused-prefill-v2 --ttl 24h --reason "p99 long-context regression; workaround"`

### 3B) Emergency runtime flag (last resort, debugging only)
If you need a one-off reproduction on a canary pod:
- Set the runtime flag via deployment override (do NOT do fleet-wide without Kernels approval):
  - `--force_kernel=fused-prefill-v2`
  - `--dump_kernel_selection=true`

This is for containment and debugging. Prefer config-based pins for production mitigation.

---

## Step 4 — Force config propagation / reload safely
Normally, changes propagate automatically. If dashboards do not reflect changes after ~5 minutes:

### 4A) Validate control plane state
- `rwctl runtime gates diff --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --model llama-3-70b-instruct`

### 4B) Trigger safe runtime config reload (no restart)
- `rwctl runtime config reload --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --service redwood-runtime`

### 4C) If pods are on stale config and reload fails
Use a **staged restart** (10% at a time). Coordinate with SRE if SLO is already violated.
- `rwctl kube rollout restart --cluster hosted-prod-us-east-1 --deploy redwood-runtime --max-unavailable 10%`

---

## Step 5 — Full rollback procedure (if needed)
A full rollback means: v2 is disabled broadly and selection behavior returns to v1.

### 5A) Rollback in Hosted (region-wide)
1. Announce in #eng-oncall and #eng-runtime: scope + reason.
2. Disable gate at region scope:
   - `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --value off`
3. If impact spans multiple regions, roll back one region at a time unless error severity requires global.
4. Validate recovery (Step 6).

### 5B) Rollback in Dedicated pools
1. Disable for the affected pool:
   - `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env dedicated --pool <pool-name> --value off`
2. Notify Customer Success owner for the account if customer-facing.

### 5C) Rollback in Private
1. Disable for tenant (managed) or provide config snippet (on-prem).
2. Request customer to confirm their workload returns to baseline.

### 5D) Rollback authority / comms
- Oncall can roll back a region/pool when SLO impact is ongoing.
- If rolling back **all Hosted prod regions**, page Runtime Kernels lead (Hiro Tanaka) and SRE oncall.
- If rollback occurs during runtime release train activity, notify Release Engineering (Connor O'Brien).

---

## Step 6 — Validate recovery (must-do)
Validation should confirm both selection behavior and user-visible SLO improvement.

### 6A) Dashboards to check (minimum)
From **Kernel Selection v2 Rollout** dashboard:
- **p95/p99 latency** by model and region (compare to 1h baseline)
- **Error rate** (runtime errors, CUDA errors, request failures)
- **Selection distribution** (should reflect v1 or the new pinned kernel distribution)
- **Fallback rate** (spikes may indicate missing kernels; acceptable short-term but investigate)

From **Serving Runtime** dashboard:
- GPU utilization and queueing
- OOM / restart counts
- Throughput (tokens/sec) stability

### 6B) Log checks
- Confirm absence of repeated selection failures:
  - `selector_v2` errors should drop if v2 is disabled
- Confirm no elevated `CUDA error` or `illegal memory access` messages

### 6C) Canary comparison (if available)
If there is an active canary cohort:
- Compare v1 vs v2 cohorts for the same model/SKU/regime
- Ensure regression is resolved before re-enabling

### 6D) Success criteria (typical)
- p99 latency returns within **+3%** of pre-event baseline (or better)
- Error rate returns to baseline (no sustained elevated CUDA/runtime errors)
- Selection distribution matches intended override

---

## Optional — Increase selector telemetry sampling (narrowly)
If you cannot attribute the regression due to low sampling:

Command (model+region scoped):
- `rwctl runtime telemetry set kernel_selection --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --model llama-3-70b-instruct --sample-rate 0.05 --ttl 2h --reason "incident triage"`

Guardrails:
- Do not exceed 5% sampling without SRE approval (cardinality + ingestion cost).
- Ensure telemetry fields do not include user prompts (PII policy).

---

## Private/on-prem config snippet (customer-facing)
If a Private on-prem customer needs a manual config override, provide this snippet (do not paste internal-only fields):

Example (YAML):
- `kernel_auto_selection_v2: "off"`

If they need a narrower override:
- `kernel_auto_selection_v2_model_overrides: "llama-3-70b-instruct=off"`

If they need a temporary pin:
- `kernel_pin: "model=llama-3-70b-instruct,gpu=nvidia-a100-80gb,seq=prefill_long,kernel=fused-prefill-v2"`

Always include:
- Scope (which model/SKU/region)
- Expected effect
- TTL / when to remove

---

## Common failure modes and recommended actions
1) **Long-context p99 spikes** (prefill > 8k)
- Action: disable v2 for model in region OR pin known-good long-prefill kernel

2) **Errors on a single SKU** (e.g., L40S)
- Action: denylist the kernel on that SKU OR disable v2 for that SKU

3) **Selection nondeterminism suspicion** (inconsistent kernel chosen for same inputs)
- Action: disable v2 for affected scope; page Runtime Architecture (Noah Patel / Jordan Lee)

4) **Dashboard alert noise due to metric cardinality**
- Action: validate actual latency/error; coordinate with Observability (Allison Grant)

---

## Post-mitigation follow-ups (required)
Within 24 hours of any production override/rollback:
1. File or update a tracking issue in the v2 epic with:
   - Scope (model/SKU/region/pool)
   - Symptoms (latency/error metrics)
   - Mitigation taken (gate off / denylist / pin)
   - Validation results
2. Update **Known Issues & Workarounds** page if this is a repeatable condition.
3. If a pin/denylist was added with TTL, set a reminder to reassess before expiry.
4. If customer-facing (Dedicated/Private), summarize in the customer ticket and share the safe removal plan.

---

## Appendix A — Reference: typical kernel names
(Names may differ by build; use the registry list command to confirm availability.)

Search runtime logs for selection event:
- `kernel_selection_v2 decision` OR `selector_v2 chosen_kernel=`

If telemetry sampling is low, temporarily increase sampling for a narrow scope (model+region) only (see "Optional: increase telemetry sampling").

---

## Step 1 — Disable v2 (narrow scope)
Disabling v2 means: selector falls back to v1 behavior.

### 1A) Disable v2 for a specific model in a region (Hosted)
Use when a single model regresses.

Command:
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --model llama-3-70b-instruct --value off`

Verify:
- `rwctl runtime gates get kernel_autoselect_v2 --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --model llama-3-70b-instruct`

Notes:
- Changes should propagate within ~2–5 minutes.
- If propagation stalls, trigger safe config reload (Step 4).

### 1B) Disable v2 for a GPU SKU in a region (Hosted)
Use when regressions are tied to a hardware type.

Command:
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --gpu-sku nvidia-l40s --value off`

### 1C) Disable v2 for a Dedicated pool
Use when a Dedicated pool has a constrained GPU type or a customer escalation.

Command:
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env dedicated --pool ded-pool-northstar-a100 --value off`

If you need to scope it further:
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env dedicated --pool ded-pool-northstar-a100 --model qwen2-72b-instruct --value off`

### 1D) Disable v2 for Private deployments
Private customers may have pinned driver/CUDA versions; treat this as customer-impacting.

Command (if customer uses managed control plane):
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env private --tenant northwind-analytics --value off`

If the customer is air-gapped/on-prem, coordinate with Support/CS and provide them the config snippet (see "Private/on-prem config snippet").

---

## Step 2 — Denylist known-bad combinations (preferred for error spikes)
Use denylisting when the issue is tied to a **kernel+SKU** combination causing errors.

Example:
- Denylist `flash-attn-v3` on `nvidia-l40s` for all models in `us-east-1`.

Command:
- `rwctl runtime kernel-registry deny --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --gpu-sku nvidia-l40s --kernel flash-attn-v3 --reason "launch failures after 1.21 canary" --ttl 72h`

Notes:
- Prefer a TTL for emergency mitigation so it is automatically revisited.
- Denylisting should force selector v2 to choose the next safe fallback; if that is insufficient, disable v2 for that SKU.

---

## Step 3 — Pin a kernel (temporary mitigation)
Pinning is a faster workaround when v2 is enabled but picking the wrong kernel for a specific regime.

**Use pinning when:**
- Latency regression is due to mis-selection, not crashes
- You have a known-good kernel from prior benchmarks

**Avoid pinning when:**
- You see runtime errors / correctness concerns
- You are unsure which kernel is safe for that SKU

### 3A) Pin by model + SKU + sequence regime bucket
Common buckets:
- `prefill_short` (<= 2k prefill tokens)
- `prefill_medium` (2k–8k)
- `prefill_long` (> 8k)
- `decode_heavy` (high decode tokens)

Command:
- `rwctl runtime kernel-pin set --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --model llama-3-70b-instruct --gpu-sku nvidia-a100-80gb --seq-bucket prefill_long --kernel fused-prefill-v2 --ttl 24h --reason "p99 long-context regression; workaround"`

### 3B) Emergency runtime flag (last resort, debugging only)
If you need a one-off reproduction on a canary pod:
- Set the runtime flag via deployment override (do NOT do fleet-wide without Kernels approval):
  - `--force_kernel=fused-prefill-v2`
  - `--dump_kernel_selection=true`

This is for containment and debugging. Prefer config-based pins for productio

description:
Context
Kernel auto-selection v2 is being rolled out behind gates. Current perf suite coverage under-represents long-context prompts (large prefill) and mixed prompt distributions that stress selector stability + batching/scheduling interactions. We also need explicit pass/fail thresholds for canary/GA decisions so we don’t debate “is this regression acceptable?” during rollout.

Goals
1) Expand benchmark coverage to include long-context and mixed workloads that match Dedicated/Private customer usage (summarization, RAG over long docs, batchy micro-prompts, and mixed prefill/decode ratios).
2) Define pass/fail thresholds for v2 vs v1 per (model family, seq-bucket regime, GPU SKU) and provide a single “canary gate” summary.
3) Ensure runs are reproducible/deterministic enough to catch tail-latency spikes (p95/p99) without flakiness.

Non-goals
- Not building a full eval/quality harness (handled by Perf & Evals separately).
- Not tuning selector thresholds here (that stays in selector PRs); this ticket only expands measurement + gating.

What to add (coverage)
A) Long-context scenarios (prefill-heavy)
- Context lengths: 8k, 16k, 32k tokens (where model supports), with decode lengths: 64, 256.
- Measure TTFT (time-to-first-token), prefill latency, and p95/p99 for first token + steady-state decode.
- Include at least one “near-memory-limit” prompt (but safe) to surface kernel choices that increase peak memory.

B) Mixed workloads (selector stability + scheduling interaction)
- Mix distributions within a single run (same worker pool):
  - 70/20/10 short/medium/long (e.g., 512/2k/16k prefill) with decode 128.
  - 50/50 interactive vs batchy (short requests with concurrency spikes vs medium requests with steady concurrency).
- Add “two-peak” distribution (most requests small, occasional very long) to replicate tail amplification.
- Ensure selector gets consistent features: model family tag, seq-bucket, GPU SKU; record selection decisions for correlation.

C) Model family coverage (minimum set for gating)
- Llama family (e.g., Llama-3 class)
- Mistral family
- Qwen family
- Gemma family
Note: the actual model IDs used in perf suite should follow the existing benchmark-lab naming + availability per GPU.

D) GPU SKUs (minimum set)
- A100 80GB
- H100 (SXM where available; PCIe acceptable if that’s what benchmark-lab has)
- L40S
- If available in lab: A100 40GB (or MIG slice) as “constrained memory” signal.

Metrics to record (must-have)
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for TTFT, end-to-end, and per-token decode (where supported).
- Throughput: tokens/sec (decode), requests/sec, and effective batch size distribution.
- Error/health: OOM rate, kernel launch failures, retried requests (if visible), and % fallback kernel usage.
- Selector telemetry correlation keys: selected_kernel, candidate_set_size, seq_bucket, gpu_sku_norm, model_family, selector_version, gate_state (v1/v2).

Pass/Fail thresholds (proposed for runtime-1.21 rollout)
Definitions
- Baseline is selector v1 on same commit (or closest stable) and same environment.
- Compare v2 vs v1 per (model family × scenario × GPU SKU). Use same seeds and at least N=5 repetitions; aggregate by median of runs for p95/p99 to reduce flake.

Hard fail (block canary expansion / trigger rollback recommendation)
- p99 end-to-end latency regression > +8% in any long-context scenario on any “supported” GPU SKU.
- p95 TTFT regression > +10% in long-context (16k/32k) scenarios.
- Error rate increase > +0.25% absolute (OOMs, launch failures) in any scenario.
- Fallback rate (to “safe” kernel) increases by > +15% absolute without corresponding error improvements (indicates mis-selection / denylist gaps).

Soft fail (requires sign-off from Runtime Architect + SRE before proceeding)
- p99 regression between +5% and +8% in any scenario.
- p95 regression between +3% and +5% in mixed workloads.
- Increased variance/run-to-run instability: coefficient of variation (CoV) for p99 > 0.12 across repetitions, u

hits.title: Fix long-context regression: adjust prefill regime thresholds to avoid tail-latency spikes
hits.text:
e 1.21, we saw a p99 regression on long-context workloads (>=16k prompt tokens) on L40S and some A100 pools when kernel auto-selection v2 classified certain requests into the “mid” prefill bucket and chose FA3 prefill variants that are great for short/mid contexts but showed allocator/workspace churn at long context (and worse tail when batch composition is mixed). This PR tightens the v2 rules to prevent mis-selection in the long-context regime while keeping determinism guarantees and preserving the gains on short/mid prompts. Changes: (1) Adjust prefill-length bucket boundaries and add a small hysteresis band to reduce flip-flopping around thresholds when scheduler-provided distribution hints are noisy. (2) Add an explicit long-context guard: for ctx >= LONG_CTX_TOKENS (default 12288), prefer the “lc_prefill” kernels when available, otherwise fall back to the known-stable v1-equivalent prefill path. (3) Add SKU-aware exception for L40S where the problematic kernel variant was disproportionately impacting tail; we now require a stricter threshold before selecting it and we prefer the stable alternative when decode_len is small (prefill-dominant requests). (4) Add unit tests covering boundary conditions + replay determinism around bucket edges, including cases with mixed scheduler hints. Bench results: See attached before/after plots from perf suite run 2026-02-14 and canary replay slice. Summary on L40S (long-context summarization profile, 16k/256): p95 1.38s -> 1.11s (-19.6%), p99 2.74s -> 1.63s (-40.5%). On A100 (same profile): p95 1.02s -> 0.98s (-3.9%), p99 1.88s -> 1.61s (-14.4%). No correctness diffs observed (golden outputs match within expected nondeterminism bounds; selection remains deterministic for fixed inputs). Notes: This is intended as a targeted rule tweak; no changes to telemetry schema. Rollout: safe to land in release/1.21 behind existing gates; recommended to promote to Hosted canary first, then Dedicated pools after 24h with the rollout dashboard guardrails. Artifacts/plots: Before/after plot bundle: gs://redwood-perf-artifacts/kernel-select-v2/28522-longctx-prefill-thresholds/plots/index.html ; Comparison table: gs://redwood-perf-artifacts/kernel-select-v2/28522-longctx-prefill-thresholds/summary.csv . Checklist: [x] Adds/updates unit tests for bucket boundaries and long-context guard [x] Verifies selector determinism tests still pass [x] Runs perf suite subset (Llama/Mistral long-context + mixed) on A100 + L40S [x] Confirms no telemetry cardinality changes [x] Updates release/1.21 notes comment (see thread) to mention long-context fix (internal) [x] Linked SUP-31842 for traceability

hits.text:
issues index
| ID | Severity | Symptom | Affected | Status | Recommended mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| KASV2-001 | High | p99 regression on long-context prefill | Llama-family long-context (>16k) on mixed fleets | Mitigated via rule tweak; watchlist | Disable v2 for model in region; or force prefill kernel fallback |
| KASV2-002 | High | Kernel crash / CUDA illegal memory access | L40S + driver 535.x + FlashAttn v3 path | Active (denylisted) | Denylist kernel on SKU+driver; pin to FA2 fallback |
| KASV2-003 | Medium | Throughput jitter on mixed workloads | H100 pools with rapidly shifting seq regime | Active (needs tuning) | Enable scheduler seq-distribution hints; increase decision cache TTL |
| KASV2-004 | Medium | Non-deterministic selection across replicas | MIG partitions / inconsistent SKU strings | Active (guardrail) | Normalize SKU; disable v2 when `gpu_partitioned=true` until normalized |
| KASV2-005 | Medium | FP8 decode instability / quality drift | H100 FP8 decode kernels on specific model variants | Active (allowlist-only) | Keep kernels allowlisted per model revision; fall back to BF16 |
| KASV2-006 | Low | Telemetry cardinality / dashboard noise | High model+kernel combinations during canary | Mitigated | Reduce sampling; aggregate candidate set; update queries |

---

## Detailed issues

### KASV2-001 — Long-context prefill mis-selection causing tail latency spikes
**Severity:** High (SLO risk)

**Symptom**
- p95 stable but **p99 spikes** (often +25–80%) for long-context workloads.
- Spikes correlate with requests where prefill tokens exceed the selector’s long-context threshold.

**Affected**
- Model families: Llama variants (including instruct), some Qwen long-context fine-tunes.
- Workload: prefill >16k tokens, or mixed traffic where the long-context share is low but impactful.
- Fleets: more pronounced on heterogeneous fleets (A100 + L40S) due to differing kernel sweet spots.

**Likely cause**
- Seq-length regime bucketing for prefill was too permissive in mixed workloads; selector chose a kernel optimized for mid-length prefill which has worse tail behavior at >16k.

**Detection signals**
- Selector telemetry shows `seq_bucket=prefill_mid` or `prefill_decode=mixed` even when observed prefill tokens are in the long bucket.
- Latency delta panel spikes only for `seq_bucket` transitions.

**Workarounds (approved)**
1) **Disable v2 for the affected model in the affected region** (preferred for immediate stabilization).
2) **Force/pin prefill kernel** for the model on the affected SKU(s) if disabling v2 is too broad.
3) **Temporary allowlist restriction**: only enable v2 for that model on GPU SKUs where long-context kernel has been validated.

**Notes / follow-ups**
- This is partially addressed by threshold updates shipped during Runtime 1.21 canary tuning. Still a watchlist item due to workload diversity.

**Last verified**: 2026-02-21

---

### KASV2-002 — L40S + driver 535.x crash on FlashAttention v3 kernel path
**Severity:** High (correctness + availability)

**Symptom**
- Occasional worker crash with:
  - `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`
  - or `misaligned address` originating from attention kernel launch.

**Affected**
- GPU SKU: L40S (not consistently reproducible on A100/H100)
- Driver/CUDA: NVIDIA 535.x (most reports on 535.129–535.161)
- Kernel family: FlashAttention v3 attention kernels (prefill + decode variants)

**Likely cause**
- Driver interaction with FA3 kernel variant under specific head dimensions / rotary embedding settings.

**Workarounds (approved)**
- **Hard denylist** the FA3 kernel variants for `gpu_sku=L40S` when `driver_major=535`.
- Fallback to FA2 or baseline attention kernels per ADR fallback precedence.
- If Dedicated/Private cannot change drivers quickly: keep denylist and plan driver upgrade.

**Operational guidance**
- If crash rate > 0.1% of requests on the pool, treat as rollback trigger for v2 on that pool.

**Last verified**: 2026-02-25

Issue summary
- Customer reports p99 latency regression for long-context summarization workloads immediately after we enabled Runtime 1.21 canary on their Dedicated pool. Regression appears only for long-context requests (>= ~16k prompt tokens) and only on NVIDIA L40S.

Impact
- Customer-visible tail latency increase on long-context routes.
- Reported baseline (Runtime 1.20 / selector v1): p99 ~4.8–5.4s @ ~20k prompt tokens, 256–512 decode tokens.
- After canary (Runtime 1.21 / selector v2 enabled): p99 ~8.9–10.6s for same workload; p50/p90 mostly unchanged.
- No correctness issues reported. Error rate stable.

Customer context
- Northwind Analytics uses Redwood Dedicated for long-context summarization (document ingestion + map-reduce style prompts). Workload is bursty but within reserved throughput.

Environment
- Dedicated pool: nw-analytics-ded-01
- Region: us-east
- GPU SKU: NVIDIA L40S (SM89)
- Driver/CUDA: 550.54.14 / CUDA 12.4
- Runtime: 1.21.0-canary.3
- Feature: Kernel auto-selection v2 enabled via canary gate for Llama family

1) Send chat.completions with large prompts (~16k–32k tokens) and max_output_tokens 256–512.
2) Observe p99 latency increase vs previous runtime.
3) Short prompts (<4k) appear unaffected.

Observed signals
- Regressions correlate with selector choosing a different prefill kernel under v2 for the LONG seq bucket on L40S.
- Telemetry shows increased time in prefill stage; decode stage stable.

content.title: Fix long-context regression: adjust prefill regime thresholds to avoid tail-latency spikes
content.text:
description:
Context: During perf characterization + Hosted canary for runtime 1.21, we saw a p99 regression on long-context workloads (>=16k prompt tokens) on L40S and some A100 pools when kernel auto-selection v2 classified certain requests into the “mid” prefill bucket and chose FA3 prefill variants that are great for short/mid contexts but showed allocator/workspace churn at long context (and worse tail when batch composition is mixed). This PR tightens the v2 rules to prevent mis-selection in the long-context regime while keeping determinism guarantees and preserving the gains on short/mid prompts. Changes: (1) Adjust prefill-length bucket boundaries and add a small hysteresis band to reduce flip-flopping around thresholds when scheduler-provided distribution hints are noisy. (2) Add an explicit long-context guard: for ctx >= LONG_CTX_TOKENS (default 12288), prefer the “lc_prefill” kernels when available, otherwise fall back to the known-stable v1-equivalent prefill path. (3) Add SKU-aware exception for L40S where the problematic kernel variant was disproportionately impacting tail; we now require a stricter threshold before selecting it and we prefer the stable alternative when decode_len is small (prefill-dominant requests). (4) Add unit tests covering boundary conditions + replay determinism around bucket edges, including cases with mixed scheduler hints. Bench results: See attached before/after plots from perf suite run 2026-02-14 and canary replay slice. Summary on L40S (long-context summarization profile, 16k/256): p95 1.38s -> 1.11s (-19.6%), p99 2.74s -> 1.63s (-40.5%). On A100 (same profile): p95 1.02s -> 0.98s (-3.9%), p99 1.88s -> 1.61s (-14.4%). No correctness diffs observed (golden outputs match within expected nondeterminism bounds; selection remains deterministic for fixed inputs). Notes: This is intended as a targeted rule tweak; no changes to telemetry schema. Rollout: safe to land in release/1.21 behind existing gates; recommended to promote to Hosted canary first, then Dedicated pools after 24h with the rollout dashboard guardrails. Artifacts/plots: Before/after plot bundle: gs://redwood-perf-artifacts/kernel-select-v2/28522-longctx-prefill-thresholds/plots/index.html ; Comparison table: gs://redwood-perf-artifacts/kernel-select-v2/28522-longctx-prefill-thresholds/summary.csv . Checklist: [x] Adds/updates unit tests for bucket boundaries and long-context guard [x] Verifies selector determinism tests still pass [x] Runs perf suite subset (Llama/Mistral long-context + mixed) on A100 + L40S [x] Confirms no telemetry cardinality changes [x] Updates release/1.21 notes comment (see thread) to mention long-context fix (internal) [x] Linked SUP-31842 for traceability

review_conversation:
Hiro Tanaka (review): The guard looks right, but I’m worried about thrash around the boundary when scheduler hints are “mostly long” but a single request is 8–10k. Can we ensure we don’t oscillate between kernels within the same warm pool? Also please justify the 12288 default. Yuki Sato (author): Added hysteresis band using a two-threshold approach when distribution_hint is present (enter long_ctx at 12k, exit at 10k) to reduce oscillation. Default 12288 matches the prefill workspace knee we saw in perf plots across L40S and A100; linked plot bundle in description. Lena Fischer (review): For mixed workloads, can you include decode_len in the guard? Some of the worst spikes were prefill-dominant. Yuki Sato: Updated rule ordering so the long_ctx guard checks (ctx_tokens >= 12288 && decode_tokens <= 512) before the generic bucket-based choice, which matches the spike signature. Omar El-Sayed (review): Please confirm we’re not changing telemetry cardinality; last week’s incident thread was noisy. Also add a log-only counter for how often this guard triggers so we can validate during rollout. Yuki Sato: No schema changes. Added a single aggregated counter kernel_select_v2.long_ctx_guard_triggered (no extra tags beyond existing model_family/gpu_sku/region sampling policy). Marcus Reed (review): Bench numbers look good, but I’d like to see at least one run on Qwen long-context profile as well. Yuki Sato: Added Qwen2.5-14B long-context run results to the same artifact bundle; deltas are neutral-to-positive (p99 -9% on L40S). Allison Grant (review): Can we add a short note to release/1.21 internal notes so oncall knows this is the fix for SUP-31842? Yuki Sato: Added a brief entry under “Kernel selection v2” in the internal known-issues/release notes file. Approvals: Hiro (approved), Lena (approved), Omar (approved), Marcus (approved).

release_notes:
Internal: Kernel auto-selection v2 adjusts long-context prefill thresholds/guard to prevent tail-latency spikes on long-context, prefill-dominant workloads (notably L40S). No user-facing config changes; controlled via existing feature gate.

content.title: Kernel Auto-Selection v2 — Override and Rollback Runbook
content.text:
## Purpose
This runbook describes how oncall can safely override or roll back **Kernel Auto-Selection v2** ("selector v2") when it causes tail-latency regressions, stability issues, or correctness risks. It covers:
- Disabling v2 by **model**, **GPU SKU**, and/or **region** (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)
- Pinning a specific kernel (temporary mitigation)
- Safe rollback procedure (fast + staged)
- Validation steps using dashboards and logs

**Primary goals:** restore p95/p99 latency and error rates to baseline while preserving correctness and preventing fleet-wide disruption.

---

## Scope / when to use
Use this runbook when any of the following are true during canary or production:
- p99 latency regression attributed to kernel selection (common: long-context prefill misclassification)
- Elevated runtime errors (CUDA illegal memory access, miscompiled kernel, launch failures) correlated with a chosen kernel/SKU
- Throughput instability or jitter that correlates with selection distribution changes
- Customer escalation requiring immediate mitigation (Dedicated/Private pools with constrained SKUs)

**Do not use** this runbook for general GPU/node instability, scheduler overload, or non-kernel runtime crashes unless kernel selection has been implicated.

---

## Ownership / escalation
**Oncall owns mitigation**, Runtime Kernels owns root cause.

- Runtime Oncall: #eng-oncall (primary)
- Runtime Kernels: #eng-runtime (paging if rollback required)
- SRE: #eng-sre (paging if SLO breach / incident)
- Releases: #eng-releases (if changes impact runtime 1.21 rollout windows)

Escalate immediately if:
- Any correctness regression suspected (bad outputs, determinism broken)
- Crash-looping exceeds 2% of pods in a region/pool
- You need to disable v2 globally in Hosted prod

---

## Preconditions / access
You need:
- Access to **Control Plane feature gates** and runtime config (prod breakglass if applicable)
- Dashboard access (Kernel Selection v2 Rollout dashboards)
- Log access for serving runtime pods

Tools referenced:
- `rwctl` (Redwood internal CLI)
- Runtime admin endpoint (read-only + safe config reload)

If `rwctl` is unavailable, use the Control Plane Console: **Console → Runtime → Feature Gates**.

---

## Definitions
- **v1**: existing kernel selection behavior (baseline)
- **v2**: kernel selection logic keyed on model family + sequence regime + GPU SKU
- **Gate**: enable/disable selector v2
- **Allowlist / denylist**: model- or SKU-scoped enablement rules
- **Pin**: force a specific kernel choice (override), bypassing selector ranking

### Canonical identifiers
Use canonical forms to avoid mismatches:
- **Region:** `us-east-1`, `us-west-2`, `eu-central-1`
- **GPU SKU:** normalized string e.g. `nvidia-a100-80gb`, `nvidia-h100-sxm`, `nvidia-l40s`
- **Model ID:** `llama-3-70b-instruct`, `mistral-large-2407`, `qwen2-72b-instruct`, `gemma-2-27b-it`

If SKU naming is ambiguous (MIG / cloud instance mapping), see: "GPU SKU normalization" in the debugging playbook.

---

## Quick decision tree (2 minutes)
1) **Is this isolated to one model OR one SKU OR one region?**
   - Yes → Disable v2 narrowly (model/SKU/region) OR pin kernel
   - No → Disable v2 at environment scope (Hosted prod or pool-wide) and page Runtime Kernels

2) **Are there runtime errors (not just latency)?**
   - Yes → Prefer **denylisting** the kernel/SKU combination (or disabling v2 for that SKU) rather than pinning.

3) **Is there a customer impact in Dedicated/Private?**
   - Yes → Prefer **pool-specific** disable or pin; avoid global Hosted changes unless needed.

---

## Primary levers
You have four safe mitigation levers (in preferred order):
1) **Disable v2 for a model in a region** (least blast radius)
2) **Disable v2 for a GPU SKU in a region/pool**
3) **Pin a kernel for a model+SKU+seq bucket** (fast workaround, higher risk)
4) **Disable v2 globally** (largest blast radius; requires notification)

---

## Step 0 — Confirm it is selector v2
Before changing gates, confirm correlation:

### A) Check selection distribution shift
Dashboard panel: **Selection distribution by kernel (model/SKU/seq bucket)**
- Look for a sudden rise in a kernel correlated with a latency spike.

### B) Confirm the request regime
Common signatures:
- Long-context prefill (e.g., prefill tokens > 8k) getting a kernel optimized for short prompts
- Mixed workloads: frequent switching between prefill/decode-heavy traffic

### C) Validate with logs (sample)
Search runtime logs for selection event:
- `kernel_selection_v2 decision` OR `selector_v2 chosen_kernel=`

If telemetry sampling is low, temporarily increase sampling for a narrow scope (model+region) only (see "Optional: increase telemetry sampling").

---

## Step 1 — Disable v2 (narrow scope)
Disabling v2 means: selector falls back to v1 behavior.

### 1A) Disable v2 for a specific model in a region (Hosted)
Use when a single model regresses.

Command:
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --model llama-3-70b-instruct --value off`

Verify:
- `rwctl runtime gates get kernel_autoselect_v2 --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --model llama-3-70b-instruct`

Notes:
- Changes should propagate within ~2–5 minutes.
- If propagation stalls, trigger safe config reload (Step 4).

### 1B) Disable v2 for a GPU SKU in a region (Hosted)
Use when regressions are tied to a hardware type.

Command:
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --gpu-sku nvidia-l40s --value off`

### 1C) Disable v2 for a Dedicated pool
Use when a Dedicated pool has a constrained GPU type or a customer escalation.

Command:
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env dedicated --pool ded-pool-northstar-a100 --value off`

If you need to scope it further:
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env dedicated --pool ded-pool-northstar-a100 --model qwen2-72b-instruct --value off`

### 1D) Disable v2 for Private deployments
Private customers may have pinned driver/CUDA versions; treat this as customer-impacting.

Command (if customer uses managed control plane):
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env private --tenant northwind-analytics --value off`

If the customer is air-gapped/on-prem, coordinate with Support/CS and provide them the config snippet (see "Private/on-prem config snippet").

---

## Step 2 — Denylist known-bad combinations (preferred for error spikes)
Use denylisting when the issue is tied to a **kernel+SKU** combination causing errors.

Example:
- Denylist `flash-attn-v3` on `nvidia-l40s` for all models in `us-east-1`.

Command:
- `rwctl runtime kernel-registry deny --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --gpu-sku nvidia-l40s --kernel flash-attn-v3 --reason "launch failures after 1.21 canary" --ttl 72h`

Notes:
- Prefer a TTL for emergency mitigation so it is automatically revisited.
- Denylisting should force selector v2 to choose the next safe fallback; if that is insufficient, disable v2 for that SKU.

---

## Step 3 — Pin a kernel (temporary mitigation)
Pinning is a faster workaround when v2 is enabled but picking the wrong kernel for a specific regime.

**Use pinning when:**
- Latency regression is due to mis-selection, not crashes
- You have a known-good kernel from prior benchmarks

**Avoid pinning when:**
- You see runtime errors / correctness concerns
- You are unsure which kernel is safe for that SKU

### 3A) Pin by model + SKU + sequence regime bucket
Common buckets:
- `prefill_short` (<= 2k prefill tokens)
- `prefill_medium` (2k–8k)
- `prefill_long` (> 8k)
- `decode_heavy` (high decode tokens)

Command:
- `rwctl runtime kernel-pin set --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --model llama-3-70b-instruct --gpu-sku nvidia-a100-80gb --seq-bucket prefill_long --kernel fused-prefill-v2 --ttl 24h --reason "p99 long-context regression; workaround"`

### 3B) Emergency runtime flag (last resort, debugging only)
If you need a one-off reproduction on a canary pod:
- Set the runtime flag via deployment override (do NOT do fleet-wide without Kernels approval):
  - `--force_kernel=fused-prefill-v2`
  - `--dump_kernel_selection=true`

This is for containment and debugging. Prefer config-based pins for production mitigation.

---

## Step 4 — Force config propagation / reload safely
Normally, changes propagate automatically. If dashboards do not reflect changes after ~5 minutes:

### 4A) Validate control plane state
- `rwctl runtime gates diff --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --model llama-3-70b-instruct`

### 4B) Trigger safe runtime config reload (no restart)
- `rwctl runtime config reload --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --service redwood-runtime`

### 4C) If pods are on stale config and reload fails
Use a **staged restart** (10% at a time). Coordinate with SRE if SLO is already violated.
- `rwctl kube rollout restart --cluster hosted-prod-us-east-1 --deploy redwood-runtime --max-unavailable 10%`

---

## Step 5 — Full rollback procedure (if needed)
A full rollback means: v2 is disabled broadly and selection behavior returns to v1.

### 5A) Rollback in Hosted (region-wide)
1. Announce in #eng-oncall and #eng-runtime: scope + reason.
2. Disable gate at region scope:
   - `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --value off`
3. If impact spans multiple regions, roll back one region at a time unless error severity requires global.
4. Validate recovery (Step 6).

### 5B) Rollback in Dedicated pools
1. Disable for the affected pool:
   - `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env dedicated --pool <pool-name> --value off`
2. Notify Customer Success owner for the account if customer-facing.

### 5C) Rollback in Private
1. Disable for tenant (managed) or provide config snippet (on-prem).
2. Request customer to confirm their workload returns to baseline.

### 5D) Rollback authority / comms
- Oncall can roll back a region/pool when SLO impact is ongoing.
- If rolling back **all Hosted prod regions**, page Runtime Kernels lead (Hiro Tanaka) and SRE oncall.
- If rollback occurs during runtime release train activity, notify Release Engineering (Connor O'Brien).

---

## Step 6 — Validate recovery (must-do)
Validation should confirm both selection behavior and user-visible SLO improvement.

### 6A) Dashboards to check (minimum)
From **Kernel Selection v2 Rollout** dashboard:
- **p95/p99 latency** by model and region (compare to 1h baseline)
- **Error rate** (runtime errors, CUDA errors, request failures)
- **Selection distribution** (should reflect v1 or the new pinned kernel distribution)
- **Fallback rate** (spikes may indicate missing kernels; acceptable short-term but investigate)

From **Serving Runtime** dashboard:
- GPU utilization and queueing
- OOM / restart counts
- Throughput (tokens/sec) stability

### 6B) Log checks
- Confirm absence of repeated selection failures:
  - `selector_v2` errors should drop if v2 is disabled
- Confirm no elevated `CUDA error` or `illegal memory access` messages

### 6C) Canary comparison (if available)
If there is an active canary cohort:
- Compare v1 vs v2 cohorts for the same model/SKU/regime
- Ensure regression is resolved before re-enabling

### 6D) Success criteria (typical)
- p99 latency returns within **+3%** of pre-event baseline (or better)
- Error rate returns to baseline (no sustained elevated CUDA/runtime errors)
- Selection distribution matches intended override

---

## Optional — Increase selector telemetry sampling (narrowly)
If you cannot attribute the regression due to low sampling:

Command (model+region scoped):
- `rwctl runtime telemetry set kernel_selection --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --model llama-3-70b-instruct --sample-rate 0.05 --ttl 2h --reason "incident triage"`

Guardrails:
- Do not exceed 5% sampling without SRE approval (cardinality + ingestion cost).
- Ensure telemetry fields do not include user prompts (PII policy).

---

## Private/on-prem config snippet (customer-facing)
If a Private on-prem customer needs a manual config override, provide this snippet (do not paste internal-only fields):

Example (YAML):
- `kernel_auto_selection_v2: "off"`

If they need a narrower override:
- `kernel_auto_selection_v2_model_overrides: "llama-3-70b-instruct=off"`

If they need a temporary pin:
- `kernel_pin: "model=llama-3-70b-instruct,gpu=nvidia-a100-80gb,seq=prefill_long,kernel=fused-prefill-v2"`

Always include:
- Scope (which model/SKU/region)
- Expected effect
- TTL / when to remove

---

## Common failure modes and recommended actions
1) **Long-context p99 spikes** (prefill > 8k)
- Action: disable v2 for model in region OR pin known-good long-prefill kernel

2) **Errors on a single SKU** (e.g., L40S)
- Action: denylist the kernel on that SKU OR disable v2 for that SKU

3) **Selection nondeterminism suspicion** (inconsistent kernel chosen for same inputs)
- Action: disable v2 for affected scope; page Runtime Architecture (Noah Patel / Jordan Lee)

4) **Dashboard alert noise due to metric cardinality**
- Action: validate actual latency/error; coordinate with Observability (Allison Grant)

---

## Post-mitigation follow-ups (required)
Within 24 hours of any production override/rollback:
1. File or update a tracking issue in the v2 epic with:
   - Scope (model/SKU/region/pool)
   - Symptoms (latency/error metrics)
   - Mitigation taken (gate off / denylist / pin)
   - Validation results
2. Update **Known Issues & Workarounds** page if this is a repeatable condition.
3. If a pin/denylist was added with TTL, set a reminder to reassess before expiry.
4. If customer-facing (Dedicated/Private), summarize in the customer ticket and share the safe removal plan.

---

## Appendix A — Reference: typical kernel names
(Names may differ by build; use the registry list command to confirm availability.)

List kernels for a SKU:
- `rwctl runtime kernel-registry list --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --gpu-sku nvidia-a100-80gb`

Common kernels:
- `flash-attn-v3`
- `triton-sdp`
- `xformers-attn`
- `fused-prefill-v2`
- `paged-kv-decode-v1`

---

## Appendix B — Safe revert of a temporary override
If you applied a temporary pin or denylist:

Remove pin:
- `rwctl runtime kernel-pin clear --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --model llama-3-70b-instruct --gpu-sku nvidia-a100-80gb --seq-bucket prefill_long`

Remove denylist entry:
- `rwctl runtime kernel-registry deny clear --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --gpu-sku nvidia-l40s --kernel flash-attn-v3`

Re-enable v2 (only after perf is validated):
- `rwctl runtime gates set kernel_autoselect_v2 --env hosted-prod --region us-east-1 --model llama-3-70b-instruct --value on`

---

## Changelog
- 2026-02-21: Added Dedicated/Private examples, TTL guidance for denylist/pins, and staged restart guidance.
- 2026-02-04: Updated telemetry sampling guardrails and validation thresholds.
- 2026-01-18: Initial version for runtime 1.21 canary and staged rollout.
